newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Aukland shares surge as rumour mill churns.
newsitem.headline: Aukland shares surge as rumour mill churns.

text.p: Shares in South African firm Aukland Investment Ltd surged again on Friday as a market rumour mill churned out speculation on a possible major acquisition and an overseas group buying into the company.
"There is a lot of speculation going on out here," one dealer said.
Aukland shares jumped 10 cents to a year high of 108 cents as nearly two million shares changed hands in morning trade.
Dealers said there was speculation in the market that the firm's medical supplies arm was on the verge of announcing an important local acquisition.

There were also rumours that an unnamed U.S. firm was about to take a minority stake in the group, possibly in conjunction with the acquisitin of some of its assets in hospital supplies. This could give the firm good accces to international markets.
"If they are getting overseas (partners) it means they will get exposure to new markets...even if it is just local it will be a big expansion locally," said one dealer.
There were also rumours about the firm securing a large export order, one dealer said.
The firm issued an announcement in September that it was in talks that may impact its share price and urged shareholders to use caution when trading in its shares.
No executives at Aukland could be contacted immediately and a spokeswoman said the firm's board was away from Johannesburg, where the group is based, at a meeting.
The group has emerged as the centre of bullish market attention this week. As late as October 7 the firm's shares were trading as low as 84 cents.
Some dealers said the shares were unlikely to go much higher until more facts were known about the potential deals. "I wouldn't personally buy at these levels," one dealer said.
But others predicted a further surge, possibly as high as 130 cents a share.
Dealers said an announcement on the deals could come as early as next week.

Aukland started out having an interest in three rent producing shopping centres and office buildings. But from July 1, 1994, the firm acquired two businesses distributing hospital and surgical equipment and related products throughout Southern Africa.
On September 27 the firm posted attributable earnings per share of 5.8 cents, up from 3.0, for the year ended June 30. Its turnover rose from 38 million rand to 66 million rand.
